Listen to this article Share South Africa’s annual inflation rate accelerated to 5.2 percent in October 2026, its highest level in more than two years, as rising prices of vegetables, fish and other food items added pressure on household budgets. Advertisement Advertisement The latest figure, released by Statistics South Africa on Wednesday, was up from 4.5 percent in September and matched the rate recorded in May 2024. The increase comes as South Africa faces uncertainty in international energy markets, with global oil prices experiencing volatility following the outbreak of the Iran war in late February. The country imports most of its fuel, leaving domestic prices exposed to movements in global energy markets. Read also: South Africa’s unemployment hits 33.7% Food and non-alcoholic beverages inflation rose for the third consecutive month to 1.4 percent in October, although lower prices for cereals and some meat products continued to limit the overall increase. Among the food categories, fish and other seafood recorded some of the sharpest price increases. Annual inflation in the category climbed to 8.4 percent in October from a recent low of 3 percent in February. Advertisement Fish fingers recorded the largest annual increase at 13.2 percent, followed by fresh and frozen hake at 11.2 percent, battered or crumbed fish at 10.1 percent and canned fish, excluding tuna, at 8.2 percent. Read also: Nigeria, South Africa, and the limits of polite diplomacy Advertisement Vegetable prices also rose sharply, with annual inflation accelerating to 8.1 percent in October from 3.5 percent in September. The category had recorded deflation of 6 percent in May. Onions were 53.6 percent more expensive than a year earlier, while potato and cabbage prices increased by 14.9 percent and 12.1 percent, respectively. Tomatoes recorded the largest monthly increase, rising by 13.2 percent between September and October. Advertisement Advertisement Prices of sugar, confectionery and desserts also increased, with the category recording annual inflation of 2.8% in October. White sugar prices rose by 3.2 percent during the month, while brown sugar increased by 2.7 percent. However, falling prices for cereals and some meat products helped contain the overall increase in food inflation. Cereal products recorded their ninth consecutive month of annual price declines, falling by 2 percent in October. Maize meal prices dropped by 9 percent compared with a year earlier, while white rice declined by 7.3 percent and brown bread by 0.8 percent. Read also: Top five things to know before buying solar power Meat inflation also eased to 0.2 percent in October from 0.7 percent in September. Stewing beef prices fell by 2.3 percent during the month, taking their annual decline to 7.7 percent. Meat bones were 6.7 percent cheaper than a year earlier, while beef mince and steak prices dropped by 4.5 percent and 4.1 percent, respectively. The figures show that while lower cereal and meat prices are providing some relief to consumers, increases in vegetables, fish and other food items are adding to the pressure on household spending. The latest acceleration also brings South Africa’s inflation rate to its highest level since May 2024, highlighting the challenge facing policymakers as they seek to contain price pressures amid uncertainty in global energy markets.
